meta.title: Velora · A coach for the day you actually had
meta.description: Velora Coach reads the Health data on your iPhone and writes short, plain notes about your steps, workouts and water. On-device, no account.
meta.ogImageAlt: Velora: a coach for the day you actually had. The Coach card says your average is 6,500 steps and suggests 7,000. Free on iPhone.

nav.ctaAria: Download Velora on the App Store

footer.disclaimer: Velora is a wellness companion, not a medical device. Consult a clinician for medical advice.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy · Velora
privacy.description: How Velora handles your data: everything stays on your device, nothing is sold, and you control every permission.

terms.title: Terms of Service · Velora
terms.description: The terms that apply when you use the Velora iOS app.

guides.indexMetaTitle: Guides on steps, water, alcohol and training · Velora
guides.indexDescription: Short, sourced answers about daily steps, water, alcohol and training, plus a steps to distance calculator.
guides.indexIntro: Short answers to everyday questions about steps, water, alcohol and training. Each guide lists its sources and the date it was last reviewed.

indexCoach.title: See these numbers for your own day
indexCoach.line: You walked 7,200 steps today, above your average.
indexCoach.body: Velora reads your steps and workouts from Apple Health and tracks your water and drinks. Velora Coach turns them into short insights and goal suggestions.

guides.note: General information, not medical advice. For questions about your own health, talk to a doctor.

hero.statusSet: Daily step goal set to 7,000. The 12:40 check-in now counts toward it.
hero.lede: Velora Coach reads the Health data already on your iPhone, then writes short, plain notes at the moments they matter. Here is one day of it.
hero.titleHtml: A coach for the day you actually had.

t0730.title: It speaks up when there is something to say.
t0730.lede: No chat window, no stream of alerts. A short note sits next to your data when there is a pattern worth pointing at.
t0730.coach: Your mornings usually carry most of your steps.
t0730.rhythmAria: Hourly steps, highest between 7 and 9 in the morning

t1240.title: Lunch, and a quick look at the count.
t1240.lede: Steps come straight from Apple Health. Velora keeps the goal you set this morning and tells you plainly where you stand.
t1240.cardNote: A walk after lunch added about 1,300.
t1240.toGoBefore: On pace for your goal, with
t1240.coach2: Your lunch walk added the most so far.

t1810.title: An evening run, read back in plain words.
t1810.lede: After a workout, Coach picks a lens for it. An easy run gets the endurance read.
t1810.coach2: Most of the run stayed in your easy zone.

t2130.title: Water and the evening glass, noted without a lecture.
t2130.lede: Intake notes describe the day next to your usual. No scores, no scolding.
t2130.coach1: Two glasses short of your usual.
t2130.coach2: A single drink logged this evening.
t2130.glassesAria: 6 of your usual 8 glasses of water

t2300.title: Today stayed on this iPhone.
t2300.localText: Your Health data is read on your device and never sent to our servers.
t2300.accountText: Open the app and go. There is nothing to sign up for.
t2300.aiText: Coach writes with Apple Intelligence on your iPhone where it is available, and uses simpler built-in lines everywhere else.
t2300.icloudText: iCloud backup is part of Pro and goes to your own iCloud account, not to us.
